candidate.educational_objective: Apply the cited evidence to recognize the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response in the clinical situation tested by V2-Q0138.

options.A: Metabolic acidosis, because the reduced pH is caused by a primary fall in bicarbonate while carbon dioxide rises only as respiratory compensation.
options.B: Respiratory alkalosis, because the elevated carbon dioxide represents excessive ventilation and the normal bicarbonate confirms alkalemia.
options.C: Acute respiratory acidosis, because acidemia is accompanied by a primary rise in PaCO₂ with little or no metabolic compensation yet apparent.
options.D: Metabolic alkalosis, because a normal bicarbonate level in an acidemic client indicates primary bicarbonate retention from renal compensation.

candidate.rationale: The ABG shows acidemia with an elevated PaCO₂ and a bicarbonate that has not risen substantially, supporting an acute primary respiratory acidosis from hypoventilation. The direction of PaCO₂, rather than a primary bicarbonate reduction or elevation, identifies the respiratory disturbance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Respiratory acidosis is a primary increase in PaCO₂ from hypoventilation, producing acidemia; acute cases initially have limited renal bicarbonate compensation.
candidate.source_locator: Merck Professional: Respiratory Acidosis — primary PaCO₂ increase from hypoventilation with acidemia; acute vs chronic compensation
candidate.stem: A somnolent client who has been hypoventilating has an ABG with pH 7.30, PaCO₂ 55 mm Hg, and HCO₃⁻ 24 mEq/L. Which acid-base interpretation is most consistent with these data?
